questions.question: What is the scientific definition of "climate"?
options: The current weather conditions measured over a single day.
The average weather conditions for a particular location over a long period of time.
The daily variation in temperature and rainfall in a specific town.
The changes in seasons that occur over the course of one year.

questions.question: What is one expected consequence of climate change on weather patterns?
options: An increase in the frequency of extreme weather events such as droughts, storms and floods.
A complete stabilization of global wind speeds and precipitation levels.
A steady decrease in the occurrence of heavy rainfall and flooding worldwide.
The elimination of seasonal changes across all continents.

questions.question: Which of the following stages in food production contributes to the carbon footprint of food?
options: Only the transportation stage from farm to shop.
Only the final packaging and retail stage.
Land-use change, farming, processing, transport, retail and packaging.
None of them, as carbon is only released during domestic cooking.

questions.question: When comparing meat and plant-based food products, what is true about their carbon footprints?
options: They have identical carbon footprints because both require farming.
Plant-based products always have a higher carbon footprint than meat.
Meat and plant-based products have different carbon footprints.
Neither meat nor plant-based products have any carbon footprint.

questions.question: How can changes in diet and a reduction in food waste help us eat more sustainably?
options: By lowering greenhouse gas emissions.
By increasing the land area needed for farming.
By encouraging the transport of foods over longer distances.
By increasing the amount of packaging required for retail.

questions.question: What is the recent, rapid increase in the Earth's average surface temperature called?
options: The carbon footprint.
Global warming.
Thermal insulation.
Sustainable development.

questions.question: What relationship do scientific data show between global temperatures and greenhouse gas emissions?
options: There is a correlation between data showing increasing temperature and data showing increasing greenhouse gas emissions.
There is no relationship at all between temperature and greenhouse gas emissions.
Temperatures are decreasing as greenhouse gas emissions increase.
Greenhouse gas emissions have decreased while temperatures have rapidly increased.

questions.question: How do thermal insulators help make a building more energy efficient?
options: They increase the amount of draft entering the building.
They generate extra heat energy inside the rooms automatically.
They reduce the energy needed to heat a building.
They prevent any light from entering through the windows.

questions.question: Why does improving a building's insulation help in using renewable resources for heating?
options: It eliminates the need for any heating system entirely.
Improving a building's insulation makes it easier to heat it using only renewable resources.
It converts non-renewable energy sources directly into solar energy.
It lowers the efficiency of solar panels and wind turbines.

questions.question: What is the primary role of thermostats in helping to reduce unnecessary heating in a home?
options: They increase the temperature difference between inside and outside.
They can control temperature automatically in different rooms and help reduce unnecessary heating.
They convert electrical energy directly into thermal insulation.
They measure the humidity levels of the outside air.

questions.question: Why do renewable resources not run out?
options: Because they are used in extremely small quantities.
Because they are replenished faster than they are used up.
Because they are created in laboratories by scientists.
Because they are completely unaffected by human consumption.

questions.question: Under what condition is wood considered a renewable resource?
options: Only if it is burned at extremely high temperatures.
Only if it is imported from tropical rainforests.
Some resources, such as wood, are only renewable if they are used sustainably.
Wood is always renewable, regardless of how it is used.

questions.question: Why is it impossible to have sustainable transport that relies on petrol or diesel fuel?
options: Because petrol and diesel cannot be purchased in large quantities.
We cannot have sustainable transport that uses petrol or diesel fuel.
Because petrol and diesel vehicles do not have any carbon emissions.
Because these fuels are replenished faster than they are used up.

questions.question: What is the role of the natural greenhouse effect on Earth?
options: It causes the surface temperature of the planet to freeze.
A natural greenhouse effect maintains optimal temperature range for life on Earth.
It prevents solar radiation from reaching the atmosphere.
It stops plants from undergoing photosynthesis.

questions.question: Why are landfill sites and incinerators major concerns for climate change?
options: They prevent the natural greenhouse effect from happening.
They are sources of greenhouse gases.
They absorb all the heat from the atmosphere.
They reduce the carbon footprint of human food production.

questions.question: What actions can we take to minimise the amount of waste we produce?
options: Increase, replace, and incinerate.
Landfill, burn, and export.
Reuse, reduce, recycle is what we can do to minimise waste.
Consume, discard, and purchase.
